toAssess.title: Preserve complete AWS placeholder names when parsing provider IDs
toAssess.why: rests on cluster-autoscaler/cloudprovider/aws/aws_cloud_provider.go:AwsRefFromProviderId, cluster-autoscaler/cloudprovider/aws/aws_cloud_provider.go:validAwsRefIdRegex, cluster-autoscaler/cloudprovider/aws/aws_cloud_provider_test.go:TestAwsRefFromProviderId; 36 changed lines in them, naming what the note names

toAssess.title: Scaleway creation errors must retain the creating state
Require Failed phase before tracking a machine as failed

findings.message: The placeholder alternative lacks a start anchor, allowing malformed IDs such as xaws:///us-east-1a/i-placeholder-some to pass validation. Extraction still assumes the ID begins with aws:///, so accepted malformed IDs also produce incorrect names.
findings.evidence: The new regex contains `$|aws\:\/\/\/[-0-9a-z]*\/%s.*$`, whereas the previous placeholder alternative began with `^aws`. Extraction uses `strings.Split(id[7:], "/")`.

locations.message: Placeholder names containing slashes are truncated. For aws:///us-east-1a/i-placeholder-some/arbitrary/cluster/local, Name becomes i-placeholder-some instead of the complete placeholder name. The change also removes the test covering this case.
locations.evidence:
splitted := strings.Split(id[7:], "/")
Name:       splitted[1],
Deleted test expected Name: "i-placeholder-some/arbitrary/cluster/local".

verdicts.reason: AWS placeholder parsing note: violation, with two demonstrated regressions. Scaleway creation-state note: unrelated. Cluster API failed-phase note: unrelated. No notes are shown to be outdated.

findings.message: The placeholder regex alternative lacks a start anchor, allowing malformed IDs with leading text to pass validation. For example, "xaws:///us-east-1a/i-placeholder-some" is accepted, and the fixed-offset parsing returns "us-east-1a" as the instance name.
findings.evidence: The new second alternative is `aws\:\/\/\/[-0-9a-z]*\/%s.*$`, without the previous `^` anchor. Validation uses `FindStringSubmatch(id)`, followed by `strings.Split(id[7:], "/")` and `Name: splitted[1]`.

findings.message: Placeholder names containing slashes are truncated. For the previously tested ID "aws:///us-east-1a/i-placeholder-some/arbitrary/cluster/local", the function now returns Name "i-placeholder-some" instead of preserving the complete placeholder name.
findings.evidence: The removed test expected Name: "i-placeholder-some/arbitrary/cluster/local". The new implementation uses `splitted := strings.Split(id[7:], "/")` and `Name: splitted[1]`.

verdicts.reason: Two bugs: slash-containing placeholder names are truncated, and malformed provider IDs with leading text are accepted and parsed incorrectly.
Note verdict: violation. The change truncates slash-containing placeholder names and accepts malformed IDs through an unanchored regex alternative. No note is outdated.

findings.message: The placeholder alternative lacks a start anchor, so malformed IDs such as junkaws:///us-east-1a/i-placeholder-some pass validation. Previously both alternatives required aws:/// at the beginning, as required by the note's invalid-format boundary.
findings.evidence:
New regex: `^aws\:\/\/\/[-0-9a-z]*\/[-0-9a-z]*(\/[-0-9a-z\.]*)?$|aws\:\/\/\/[-0-9a-z]*\/%s.*$`
Previous placeholder alternative: `^aws\:\/\/\/[-0-9a-z]*\/(%s.*)$`
Validation rejects only when validAwsRefIdRegex.FindStringSubmatch(id) == nil.

locations.message: Placeholder names containing slashes are truncated. For aws:///us-east-1a/i-placeholder-some/arbitrary/cluster/local, Name becomes i-placeholder-some instead of the complete placeholder name, violating the note's preservation requirement.
locations.evidence:
splitted := strings.Split(id[7:], "/")
Name:       splitted[1],
Deleted test expected Name: "i-placeholder-some/arbitrary/cluster/local".

findings.verified: The placeholder alternative lost its leading ^, so FindStringSubmatch can match aws:/// after arbitrary leading text. Previously both alternatives were anchored. Such malformed IDs now pass validation and are parsed incorrectly because extraction still assumes aws:/// starts at offset zero.

integrity.limitation: Pattern-based signals do not establish equivalent coverage or detect every weakened gate.
